h1: Fruit of the Loom underwear and socks in Europe — what is sold, sizes and prices
intro: In the United States Fruit of the Loom is an underwear brand first; in Europe the catalogue is built around T-shirts and sweats, with underwear, socks and tank tops sold as basics alongside. Here is what you can actually buy in Europe in 2026, what it costs in EUR, how the sizes work and how to make it last.

body_html:
Does Fruit of the Loom sell underwear in Europe?

Yes, but the range looks different from the one Americans know. In the United States, Fruit of the Loom is first and foremost an underwear brand — multipacks of boxer briefs, briefs and undershirts have been supermarket staples for generations, and the label itself dates back to 1871, one of the oldest trademarks in the country. In Europe, where the brand is run by Fruit of the Loom International from Kaiserslautern in Germany, the catalogue is built around T-shirts, sweats and polos for retail and printing. Underwear and socks are sold as basics alongside that range: plain cotton underwear in small packs, unisex socks and tank tops and tees that double as undershirts.

That is worth knowing before you search, because the big US-style 6-packs of boxer briefs are mostly not what you will find on European shelves. What you will find is cheap, plain, cotton-rich basics from the same factory network that makes the tees.

How does Fruit of the Loom underwear compare with other brands?

The brand's pitch has not changed in 170 years: plain, comfortable cotton basics at a low price, made in large volumes so the quality is consistent from pack to pack. Compared with designer underwear from brands such as Calvin Klein or Tommy Hilfiger, you are paying a fraction of the price and giving up mainly the logo on the waistband; day-to-day comfort in a cotton-rich fabric is comparable. Compared with supermarket and fast-fashion own-brand packs, Fruit of the Loom's advantage is consistency — the same cut, the same colours and the same sizes are available year after year, so you can re-order the pair you like.

  • Best for: people who want plain black or grey cotton basics at around €5 per pair and do not care about branding.
  • Not for: anyone who wants a wide choice of prints, patterns, sports-specific trunks or premium modal fabrics — that is not what this range is.

Which size should you order?

Fruit of the Loom underwear fits true to size for most people: take the size you wear in the brand's T-shirts. If you are between sizes, go up for underwear and stay with your usual size for tank tops. Socks are sold in shoe-size bands, which makes them easy to buy for someone else.

Socks: 35–38, 39–42, 43–46 and 47–50 (EU shoe sizes). If the retailer's product page shows its own chart, follow that — waist bands above are a guide only. The full charts for tees, sweats and kids are in our {{LINK:size-guide|Fruit of the Loom size guide}}.

Tank tops and T-shirts as undershirts: the European way

Because the European catalogue is built around tees, the most common Fruit of the Loom "underwear" purchase here is actually a plain white or black tank top or Valueweight T worn under a shirt. At €5.95–6.95 each, or €6.26 for the tee when you buy five, they are cheaper than most dedicated undershirts and come in sizes up to 3XL. The Valueweight T at approx. 165 g/m² is light enough to disappear under a shirt; the {{SHOP:/products/fruit-of-the-loom-v-neck-t-shirt|V-neck T-shirt}} is the classic choice under an open collar. Both are covered in our {{LINK:t-shirts|Fruit of the Loom T-shirt guide}}, and the tank tops in the {{LINK:shorts-summer|shorts and summer basics guide}}.

How should you wash Fruit of the Loom underwear and socks?

  • Wash at 40 °C with ordinary detergent; avoid bleach, which weakens elastic.
  • Separate dark and light. Black socks and underwear with the dark load, white tank tops with the whites.
  • Skip the hot tumble dryer. Heat is what kills elastic. Air drying or a low setting doubles the life of a waistband.
  • No ironing needed. Cotton underwear and socks come out of a normal spin fine.
  • Replace on a schedule. When a waistband loosens or a sock heel goes thin, it is time — at €2.95 per pair there is no reason to keep worn-out socks.

Where should you buy Fruit of the Loom underwear and socks in Europe?

The range is small and the prices are low, so it rarely makes sense to shop around for underwear alone. The practical approach is to add socks, underwear or tank tops to an order of T-shirts or a hoodie and let the quantity discount and the single €7 shipping fee do the work. The cheapest verified option is Marmalade Co., which buys directly from the Fruit of the Loom factory in Morocco, ships from Denmark with DHL in 2–3 business days and runs a price guarantee on identical products. Amazon marketplaces and the official fruitoftheloom.eu shop also list basics; see our overview of {{LINK:where-to-buy|where to buy Fruit of the Loom in Europe and Ireland}} for the full list of verified shops.

faq.q: Does Fruit of the Loom sell boxers and briefs in Europe?
faq.a: Only as a small basics range. The classic US multipacks of boxer briefs and briefs are mostly not sold through European retailers; instead you will find plain men's underwear in 2-packs (€9.95 at Marmalade Co., black or dark grey, S–XL and up), unisex socks and tank tops. Check size and pack details on the product page before ordering.

faq.q: How much do Fruit of the Loom socks cost?
faq.a: The cheapest verified price in Europe is €2.95 per pair at Marmalade Co. in black or white, sizes 35–38, 39–42, 43–46 and 47–50 (approx., September 2026). Buying three pairs gives 5 % off and five or more gives 10 % off, and they ship with a flat €7 DHL fee together with anything else in the order.

faq.q: Is Fruit of the Loom underwear 100 % cotton?
faq.a: The brand's basics are cotton-rich, and premium lines use combed cotton with an OEKO-TEX certificate shown on product pages. Underwear with a stretch waistband typically contains a small share of elastane, so check the composition on the product page for the exact pack. Tank tops and the Valueweight T used as undershirts are 100 % cotton.

faq.q: What size Fruit of the Loom underwear should I buy?
faq.a: Take the size you wear in the brand's T-shirts: S fits an 89–94 cm chest, M 95–100 cm, L 101–106 cm and XL 107–112 cm, which correspond roughly to waists of 76–82, 82–90, 90–98 and 98–106 cm. If you are between sizes, go up for underwear. Socks are sold by EU shoe size band, for example 43–46.

faq.q: Can I use a Fruit of the Loom T-shirt as an undershirt?
faq.a: Yes, and in Europe that is the most common use. The Valueweight T at approx. 165 g/m² is light enough to sit under a shirt, costs €6.95 (€6.26 each at 5+) and comes in white, black and 14 other colours up to 3XL. The V-neck T-shirt is the classic choice under an open collar; tank tops from €5.95 are the lightest option.

faq.q: How do I stop underwear elastic from wearing out?
faq.a: Heat is the main enemy. Wash at 40 °C without bleach, avoid hot tumble drying and air dry instead, and wash darks separately so black underwear and socks keep their colour. Treated this way the waistband outlasts the fabric. Replace a pair when the band loosens — at these prices there is no reason to keep worn-out basics.
